item.title: Exploited GitLab RCE, European Freezer Attacks, and DarkBlinders Intrusions
item.content:encoded:
Window: 02 Nov 11:00 → 02 Nov 15:00 UTC (4 hours)

Over 1,000 GitLab servers vulnerable to ongoing RCE attacks — Must Read

More than 1,000 internet-exposed GitLab servers remain unpatched against CVE-2026-97229, a maximum-severity unauthenticated RCE flaw that CISA says is actively being exploited. Self-managed GitLab users should immediately upgrade to versions 19.4.2, 19.3.5, or 19.2.8.

  • CVE-2026-97229 is a maximum-severity GitLab flaw that can allow an unauthenticated user to execute arbitrary code through a specially crafted regular expression in a CI/CD configuration.
  • GitLab released patches for CVE-2026-97229 in GitLab CE and EE versions 19.4.2, 19.3.5, and 19.2.8, and said GitLab.com is already patched.
  • CISA confirmed that CVE-2026-97229 is being exploited in the wild and added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog.
  • Shadowserver reported that it tracked more than 1,000 internet-exposed GitLab instances vulnerable to CVE-2026-97229 three weeks after patches became available.
  • Shadowserver also reported more than 11,300 GitLab instances vulnerable to CVE-2026-110264 out of roughly 39,000 GitLab instances it sees daily.

Technologies: ci-cd, source-control

Products: gitlab-ce, gitlab-ee, gitlab-cicd-regular-expression-compiler

Vendors: gitlab

Synology warns of C3RB3R ransomware attacks targeting NAS devices — Must Read

Synology is urging NAS owners to immediately update DiskStation Manager and disable Internet access to its management interface after C3RB3R ransomware attackers began exploiting a vulnerability patched in December 2024 to encrypt data on unpatched devices.

  • Synology warned that C3RB3R ransomware actors are exploiting a vulnerability patched in December 2024 to target NAS devices running outdated DiskStation Manager versions.
  • Synology urged users to update DiskStation Manager immediately, enable automatic updates, and block internet access to the management web interface.
  • The November 2024 advisory linked by Synology describes fixes for CVE-2024-10441, CVE-2024-50629, and CVE-2024-10445, which could allow arbitrary code execution, file reading, or file writing on unpatched devices.
  • Affected users reported that the ransomware adds a .L0CK3D extension to encrypted files and leaves a read-me3.txt ransom note directing victims to purchase a C3rb3r Decryptor.
  • Shadowserver tracks more than 380,000 internet-exposed Synology NAS devices, though it does not report how many are patched or honeypots.

Technologies: nas, operating-system

Products: diskstation-manager

Vendors: synology

Critical Langflow Flaws Could Let Unauthenticated Attackers Run Code on Servers — Should Read

Langflow versions 1.0.0 through 1.12.8 contain critical flaws that can let unauthenticated remote attackers bypass authentication or execute arbitrary code, including through MCP tool enumeration. Organizations should upgrade to Langflow 1.13.0 immediately, as IBM provides no workaround.

  • IBM reported that Langflow versions 1.0.0 through 1.12.8 are affected by four vulnerabilities, including two critical issues rated 9.8.
  • CVE-2026-93680 can allow unauthenticated attackers to bypass authentication, while CVE-2026-110186 can allow unauthenticated arbitrary code execution through Model Context Protocol tool enumeration.
  • A public Metasploit Framework module for CVE-2026-93680 can connect to a Langflow server's MCP endpoint without credentials and list its available tools.
  • Langflow 1.13.0, released October 22, fixes the flaws, turns automatic login off by default, and is the only remediation IBM provides for affected deployments.
  • IBM also published 29 additional Langflow CVE records on October 29, including CVE-2026-104339, an unauthenticated arbitrary-code-execution issue rated 9.8.

Products: langflow, metasploit-framework

Vendors: ibm, langflow, rapid7

Attackers Pose as IT Support on Microsoft Teams, Abuse AD CS to Steal Company Data — Should Read

Attackers impersonated IT support in Microsoft Teams to trick employees into granting Quick Assist access, then abused misconfigured Active Directory Certificate Services to obtain privileged certificates, access domain controllers, and steal data. The incidents underscore that securing AD CS templates and web enrollment, restricting remote-support access, and fully containing compromised identities are critical.

  • Attackers impersonated company IT or help-desk staff in Microsoft Teams and convinced employees to share Quick Assist connection codes, giving the attackers control of their workstations.
  • Microsoft investigated two intrusions in which attackers abused insecure Active Directory Certificate Services configurations to obtain certificates for privileged accounts, including a domain controller.
  • In one case, attackers exploited an ESC1 certificate template weakness, used DCSync against a domain controller, and copied company data from a file server to an external SFTP server using a renamed Rclone tool.
  • In the other case, attackers used PetitPotam and an ESC8 NTLM relay to obtain a domain controller certificate, but Defender alerts and workstation isolation stopped further activity.
  • Microsoft said the activity exploited social engineering and insecure configuration rather than a flaw in Microsoft Teams, and it was not attributed to a known group.

Technologies: remote-access, iam, edr, operating-system

Products: microsoft-teams, quick-assist, active-directory-certificate-services, microsoft-defender-for-endpoint, microsoft-defender-for-identity, windows-server

Vendors: microsoft

DarkBlinders Compromises Israeli Target and Iraqi Kurdish Government Cloud Environment — Should Read

Iran-aligned DarkBlinders targeted a high-profile Israeli individual and a Kurdistan Regional Government cloud environment using tailored phishing, fake software and recruitment lures to deploy ShelbyLoader and ShelbyC2. Researchers assess the activity may be linked to broader Iran-nexus clusters associated with APT34.

  • Dream Research Labs reported that Iran-aligned DarkBlinders compromised a high-profile individual in Israel and a government cloud environment in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq between August and October 2026.
  • DarkBlinders used targeted phishing, lookalike government, webmail, and cloud-service domains, fake recruitment offers, and a counterfeit StarkMeet videoconferencing application to collect credentials or deliver malicious files.
  • The group’s infection chain used a malicious Visual Studio project, AppDomainManager injection, and DLL sideloading to deploy ShelbyLoader V2, ShelbyC2, and the Blackwood tunneling utility.
  • Dream assessed with medium confidence that DarkBlinders activity overlaps operationally with UNC5795 and Dust Specter, with potential links to sub-clusters associated with APT34.
  • Separately, the Iranian government-sponsored Prince of Persia group was observed operating a U.S.-hosted command-and-control server in 2026 after a three-month period of inactivity.

Technologies: source-control

Products: visual-studio, github, telegram

Vendors: microsoft, github, telegram

Hackers disrupt refrigeration systems at European supermarkets — Should Read

A cyberattack remotely altered refrigeration controls at more than 115 supermarkets and shops across several European countries, causing freezers to shut down, defrost, or heat up and leading to product losses. The incidents may exploit the same weakness used in recent attacks on French stores’ refrigeration controllers.

  • A cyberattack disrupted refrigeration and freezer systems at more than 115 stores in Belgium, the Netherlands, Sweden, Luxembourg, Ireland, and Estonia.
  • Affected equipment was reported to have been shut down, switched to defrost mode, or in one case begun generating heat, causing rising temperatures and product losses.
  • The affected chains include ICA, Coop, Ahold Delhaize, Carrefour, Spar Colruyt, Intermarché, SuperValu, and Selver, while additional Dutch butcher shops and neighborhood stores were also impacted.
  • An ICA store manager said temperature settings were changed overnight to 50°C and could not be modified, forcing the store to discard frozen food.
  • Sabcobel director Stephan Moelans said the attacker used the same weakness involved in similar refrigerator attacks in France the previous month, and that remote activation of defrost functions caused the disruption.

Technologies: ics-scada, iot-device

Products: danfoss-ak-sm, danfoss-ak-sc, copeland-dixell-xweb

Vendors: sabcobel, danfoss, copeland, dixell

Apple warns users in 99 countries of mercenary spyware — Should Read

Apple issued mercenary-spyware threat notifications to targeted users in 99 countries, including journalists in Turkey and Lebanon. The alerts are not attributed to a specific actor, but highlight continuing sophisticated surveillance of investigative reporters.

  • Apple sent a new round of threat notifications warning targeted users in 99 countries about suspected mercenary spyware attacks.
  • Recipients who publicly disclosed notifications include Turkey-based Middle East Eye bureau chief Ragıp Soylu and Lebanese journalist and documentary filmmaker Radwan Mortada.
  • Apple said it does not attribute these attacks to particular actors or regions because mercenary spyware campaigns are costly, sophisticated, and global.
  • Mortada said his phone was previously targeted with Pegasus zero-click spyware in 2017 and 2021.
  • Apple had not publicly posted the latest notifications on its website and did not respond to a request for comment.

Products: apple-threat-notifications

Vendors: apple

Russian and Ukrainian hackers hijack emergency apps to spread fake nuclear attack warnings — Should Read

Hackers compromised Ukraine’s Air Alert app and Russia’s EMERCOM emergency app to send false nuclear, radiation, and attack warnings, though both countries said their primary public-warning systems remained unaffected. The incidents highlight how emergency-notification apps can be exploited for wartime disinformation and panic.

  • Ukraine’s Air Alert app was likely compromised, causing Kyiv residents to receive fake notifications about radiation, chemical threats, street fighting, and a possible Oreshnik missile strike.
  • The Air Alert developers disabled push notifications and temporarily suspended the service before gradually restoring basic alerts with additional security measures.
  • A group calling itself DC8044 claimed it accessed Russia’s EMERCOM emergency app and used it to distribute false warnings that nuclear warheads had been launched toward Russia.
  • Russia’s Emergency Situations Ministry acknowledged that its mobile app had been hacked but said its primary public-warning infrastructure, including sirens, loudspeakers, text messages, television, and radio, was unaffected.
  • Ukrainian authorities said the national warning system and Kyiv Digital app remained operational despite the compromise of the Air Alert app.

Products: air-alert, emercom, kyiv-digital

Vendors: ajax-systems, ministry-of-emergency-situations-russia

Microsoft fixes Smart App Control broken by October Windows update — May Read

Microsoft fixed an issue caused by the October 2026 KB5127648 Windows 11 update that left Smart App Control grayed out and unable to be enabled. The fix is available in the KB5127936 preview update, with registry and Group Policy workarounds for organizations that defer it.

  • Microsoft resolved an issue in which the October 2026 KB5127648 Windows 11 security update prevented some users from enabling Smart App Control.
  • The issue affected Windows 11 24H2 and later devices where Smart App Control had been turned off, leaving the option grayed out, while devices with it already enabled remained protected.
  • Microsoft said the fix is included in Windows updates released on October 28, 2026 and later, including the KB5127936 preview update.
  • Organizations that do not want to deploy the preview update can use Microsoft-provided registry commands or Group Policy settings as a temporary workaround.
  • The KB5127936 preview update also addresses Remote Desktop failures tied to Administrator protection and Always On VPN issues triggered by September 2026 cumulative updates.

Technologies: operating-system, antivirus, remote-access, vpn

Products: windows-11, smart-app-control, windows-security, microsoft-defender, smartscreen, remote-desktop, always-on-vpn

Vendors: microsoft

Backporting security fixes at scale with Codex — May Read

Trail of Bits says its Codex-assisted workflow can reduce the human effort to backport security fixes into stable Linux releases from days to hours, helping address thousands of known CVEs that remain unpatched in long-term-supported software. The project has already helped land fixes for 149 CVEs in stable Linux kernel branches and is extending the effort to Fedora and Ubuntu packages.

  • Trail of Bits says its Codex workflow uses agents to identify missing fixes, adapt patches for older code, run tests, assemble validation evidence, and prepare submission packets for human review.
  • The project reports that, by October 29, it helped deliver fixes for 149 distinct CVEs into stable Linux kernel releases and submitted several fixes for Fedora and Ubuntu packages.
  • For a straightforward backport, Trail of Bits estimates that patch preparation and review require about 30 minutes of human attention, while more involved cases can require around three hours.
  • The article reports that supported Linux kernel stable branches had hundreds to thousands of known CVEs fixed in newer branches but still unfixed in the older branch, based on the kernel CVE team’s data as of September 18, 2026.
  • Trail of Bits emphasizes that regression testing and acceptance by package and kernel maintainers remain necessary even when AI reduces the effort required to prepare a backport.

Technologies: operating-system

Products: codex, gpt-5-6, linux-kernel, ubuntu-26-04-lts, debian-13, fedora

Vendors: trail-of-bits, openai, canonical, red-hat, debian-project, linux-kernel-project

Is Your SOC Ready for AI Agents? A Maturity Check Before You Deploy — Optional

SOC teams should assess data access, investigation standards, human-approval rules, and baseline metrics before deploying AI agents. The sponsored article positions Prophet Security’s AI SOC platform as a way to automate alert investigations, hunting, and detection engineering while retaining human oversight.

  • Prophet Security’s survey of more than 250 security leaders and practitioners found that 40% of security teams use AI daily, 56% are testing it, and 4% have no adoption plans.
  • The article says AI SOC agents can investigate alerts as they arrive by querying connected security tools and documenting the evidence behind their conclusions.
  • Before deploying an AI agent, the article recommends ensuring it has API access to relevant data sources, readable business context, healthy data pipelines, written investigation standards, and defined approval rules.
  • The article states that 28% of alerts are never investigated and that a thorough investigation takes an average of 75 minutes, according to its cited survey.
  • The article promotes Prophet AI as a platform with agents for alert investigation, threat hunting, and detection engineering, with customer-controlled permissions and human approval as the default for response actions.

Technologies: siem, edr, identity-provider, cloud-platform, email-security

Products: prophet-ai, prophet-ai-soc-analyst, prophet-ai-threat-hunter, prophet-ai-detection-engineer

Vendors: prophet-security

item.title: Ivanti Connect Secure Zero-Day Chain, Linux TCP RCE, and CyberStrikeAI Attacks
item.content:encoded:
Window: 02 Nov 07:00 → 02 Nov 11:00 UTC (4 hours)

Ivanti patches two more Connect Secure zero-days chained in attacks — Must Read

Ivanti patched two additional Connect Secure zero-days, CVE-2026-111357 and CVE-2026-118527, that attackers chained with a previously patched authentication bypass to obtain unauthenticated root-level access. Administrators should urgently update exposed appliances, as exploitation has been observed since early October.

  • Ivanti released patches for CVE-2026-111357, a high-severity privilege-escalation flaw, and CVE-2026-118527, which allows authenticated attackers to upload files to unpatched Connect Secure devices.
  • Attackers chained these two flaws with the previously patched CVE-2026-104935 authentication bypass to obtain unauthenticated root-level code execution on fully patched Connect Secure devices.
  • Volexity reported that the threat actor UTA0576 had used the vulnerability chain since at least October 3 and repeatedly re-exploited devices for commands while tampering with logs.
  • CISA added CVE-2026-104935 to its catalog of actively exploited vulnerabilities and directed U.S. federal agencies to patch affected systems by Friday.
  • Shadowserver tracks more than 5,000 Internet-exposed Ivanti Connect Secure instances, although the number secured against the ongoing attacks is unknown.

Technologies: vpn, remote-access

Products: connect-secure

Vendors: ivanti

Critical Linux kernel TCP vulnerability can allow remote code execution (CVE-2026-98432) — Must Read

CVE-2026-98432 is a critical Linux kernel IPv4 TCP use-after-free flaw that may enable unauthenticated remote code execution on reachable MPTCP-enabled services. Install your vendor’s patched kernel and reboot immediately; disabling MPTCP and filtering IPv4 IP options are only temporary mitigations.

  • CVE-2026-98432 is a Linux kernel IPv4 TCP use-after-free flaw affecting kernel version 4.4 and later, which the kernel CVE team rates 9.8 out of 10.
  • Anthropic reported that an unreleased Claude research model produced an exploit that achieved root-level command execution on a Linux server with an MPTCP listener.
  • Installing a vendor-patched kernel and rebooting is the complete remediation, while disabling MPTCP or dropping IPv4 packets with IP options are temporary exposure-reduction measures.
  • Internet-reachable Linux hosts, including EC2 instances, ECS container instances, and EKS nodes, are affected when they expose an IPv4 TCP port; the container host kernel is what matters for containers.
  • No vendor advisory had reported exploitation in the wild as of October 29, 2026.

Technologies: operating-system, cloud-platform, container-platform, orchestration

Products: linux-kernel, amazon-linux-2, amazon-linux-2023, amazon-eks, amazon-ecs, aws-fargate, bottlerocket, ubuntu, red-hat-enterprise-linux, debian, oracle-linux, suse-linux-enterprise-server, cloudlinux-os, golang

Vendors: linux-kernel-project, anthropic, aws, aikido, canonical, red-hat, debian-project, oracle, suse, cloudlinux, google

CyberStrikeAI in the wild: the use of AI in real-world attacks on organizations — Should Read

Kaspersky documented a real-world campaign against education-sector organizations in Africa and Latin America in which attackers used the open-source CyberStrikeAI framework to have a server-side LLM orchestrate post-exploitation actions through conventional C2 implants. The AI did not introduce novel on-host techniques, but accelerated familiar domain-compromise steps including reconnaissance, credential dumping, lateral movement, and data collection.

  • Kaspersky identified a campaign targeting education-sector organizations in several countries across Africa and Latin America that used the open-source CyberStrikeAI framework during post-exploitation.
  • CyberStrikeAI uses a server-side large language model to plan actions, select tools, and generate commands, while a conventional implant on compromised hosts executes those commands.
  • In one incident, attackers moved from deploying the CyberStrikeAI agent to persistence and local reconnaissance within two minutes, domain reconnaissance over five hours, and lateral movement, credential dumping, and database export within about one hour during the final stage.
  • The attackers used familiar techniques including scheduled tasks, PowerShell, WMI, SMB, LSASS memory dumping, DCSync, Golden Ticket attacks, and SQL and LDAP queries.
  • Kaspersky could not link the activity to a known threat group, although Chinese-language script comments, use of Chinese services, and server restart timing suggested a possible Chinese-speaking operator.

Technologies: edr, siem, network-monitoring, database, antivirus

Products: cyberstrikeai, kaspersky-next-edr-expert, kaspersky-anti-targeted-attack, kaspersky-siem, sql-server, microsoft-defender

Vendors: kaspersky, microsoft, aipentest

item.title: VOLTA Infostealer Uses Claude, Gemini, and Kimi to Monetize Stolen Data
item.content:encoded:
Window: 02 Nov 03:00 → 02 Nov 07:00 UTC (4 hours)

New VOLTA Infostealer Uses Claude, Gemini, and Kimi AI to Rank Victims by Financial Value — Should Read

Researchers uncovered VOLTA-AUTODOXER, a Windows infostealer that uses Claude, Kimi, or Gemini through OpenRouter to turn stolen credentials and personal data into ranked, monetization-focused victim dossiers. The malware exfiltrates data and AI-generated assessments via Telegram, illustrating how criminals are using LLMs to automate victim triage.

  • Cisco Talos identified VOLTA-AUTODOXER, a Windows information-stealing program that collects browser credentials and cookies, payment cards, cryptocurrency wallet phrases, application sessions, cloud and SSH keys, Wi-Fi profiles, and screenshots.
  • VOLTA creates a structured profile containing information such as location, home address, employer, payment-card last four digits, Slack workspaces, document metadata, iPhone backup indicators, and Roblox account value.
  • The malware uses stolen Gmail session access to search for receipts from services including Amazon, DoorDash, Uber Eats, Grubhub, Walmart, and PayPal to support home-address information.
  • VOLTA sends collected data to AI models through OpenRouter, defaulting to Claude Opus 4.6 and falling back to Kimi K2 or Gemini 2.5 Flash if a model refuses the request.
  • The AI-generated output ranks valuables by potential monetization and assesses the victim's security habits, while VOLTA sends data and analysis results to Telegram at multiple stages.

Technologies: api-gateway, remote-access

Products: volta-autodoxer, nik-c2, openrouter, claude-opus-4-6, kimi-k2, gemini-2-5-flash, gmail, microsoft-outlook, telegram

Vendors: cisco, anthropic, moonshot-ai, google, openrouter, openai, microsoft, telegram, zscaler

item.title: FBI Attributes $6.3 Billion Binance Heist to North Korea’s TraderTraitor
item.content:encoded:
Window: 01 Nov 19:00 → 01 Nov 23:00 UTC (4 hours)

FBI links $6.3 billion Binance crypto heist to North Korean hackers — Must Read

The FBI attributed the record $6.3 billion Binance cryptocurrency theft to North Korean TraderTraitor/Lazarus hackers, who allegedly gained access through a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop. Binance says it has covered about 95% of affected assets and plans to resume withdrawals while authorities seek to block laundering addresses.

  • The FBI attributed the theft of more than $6 billion in virtual assets from Binance on October 29, 2026, to North Korean state-sponsored hackers known as TraderTraitor, also tracked as Lazarus Group, Jade Sleet, and APT38.
  • Binance said attackers used a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop to access a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions, stealing approximately $6.36 billion across ten blockchains.
  • The FBI reported that the group has primarily converted the stolen assets into Ethereum and may further launder them through decentralized finance platforms and instant cryptocurrency swap services.
  • The FBI published 628 cryptocurrency addresses associated with the theft and asked exchanges, blockchain operators, and virtual asset service providers to block transactions linked to those addresses.
  • Binance said it had covered approximately 95% of the affected amount, would bear the financial losses rather than pass them to users, and planned to resume the first phase of withdrawals on November 1.

Vendors: binance

item.title: Alpine Linux Rebuilds GitLab After CVE-2026-97229 RCE Exploitation Attempt
item.content:encoded:
Window: 01 Nov 15:00 → 01 Nov 19:00 UTC (4 hours)

Alpine Linux rebuilds GitLab after attempted RCE attack — Must Read

Alpine Linux rebuilt its GitLab infrastructure and reset passwords after attackers attempted to exploit the critical CVE-2026-97229 GitLab RCE flaw. No compromise was confirmed, but incomplete logs meant the project could not rule out code execution or exposure of GitLab data and secrets.

  • Attackers attempted to exploit CVE-2026-97229 against Alpine Linux’s GitLab development infrastructure on October 20–21, causing eight worker-process crashes.
  • CVE-2026-97229 is a maximum-severity GitLab remote-code-execution flaw involving the Onigmo regular-expression compiler bundled with Ruby.
  • Alpine Linux initially deployed unpatched GitLab versions, and its custom container image lacked the Ruby patch required to fix the flaw even after an upgrade to GitLab 19.3.6.
  • Alpine found no evidence of altered commits, packages, or releases through October 27, but rebuilt its GitLab instance because missing logs prevented it from ruling out code execution.
  • Alpine advised GitLab users to reset their passwords and use the alpinelinux/gitlab:19.3.6 image published October 27, which includes Ruby 3.3.13 and addresses the flaw.

Technologies: operating-system, container-platform, ci-cd, source-control

Products: alpine-linux, gitlab, onigmo, ruby

Vendors: alpine-linux, gitlab

item.title: Critical LXD CVE-2026-112816, Binance Heist Attribution, and NetamLoader Campaign
item.content:encoded:
Window: 01 Nov 07:00 → 01 Nov 11:00 UTC (4 hours)

FBI Links North Korea's TraderTraitor to Record $6.43 Billion Binance Crypto Heist — Must Read

The FBI attributed the record $6.43 billion Binance cryptocurrency theft to North Korea-linked TraderTraitor (Jade Sleet), with attackers converting much of the stolen assets to Ethereum for laundering. About $2.85 billion has been frozen, while Binance has begun gradually restoring withdrawals after the incident.

  • The FBI attributed the theft of more than $6 billion in virtual assets from Binance to the North Korea-aligned TraderTraitor group, also known as Jade Sleet and several other names.
  • U.S. agencies observed the attackers converting stolen assets primarily into Ethereum, which the FBI said could be further laundered through decentralized finance and instant-swap services.
  • The $6.43 billion theft surpassed the $1.46 billion taken from Bybit in February 2025, making it the largest cryptocurrency theft in history according to the article.
  • Tether, Circle, Ripple, Arbitrum, and Optimism froze $2.85 billion of the $6.43 billion stolen assets on-chain.
  • Binance resumed the first phase of withdrawals after pausing them following the incident, while deposit services remained open.

Products: terraform

Vendors: binance, hashicorp, tether, circle, ripple, arbitrum, optimism

CVSS 10.0 LXD, MicroCloud Flaw Lets Attackers Impersonate Trusted Clients Without a Private Key — Should Read

Canonical patched CVE-2026-112816, a CVSS 10.0 LXD and MicroCloud flaw that lets network-reachable attackers impersonate trusted mTLS clients using only their public certificates. Update LXD and MicroCloud immediately and restrict HTTPS API access until patched.

  • CVE-2026-112816 is a CVSS 10.0 flaw in Canonical LXD and MicroCloud that can allow an attacker to impersonate a trusted client without its private key.
  • The issue occurs because the server checked every certificate supplied by a client against its trust store, even though the connection proves ownership only of the private key for the first certificate.
  • Exploitation requires network access to the HTTPS API and a public certificate for a client that the server already trusts.
  • Canonical released fixed LXD versions 6.10.1, 5.21.9, 5.0.11, and 4.0.15, plus MicroCloud versions 3.4.1 and 2.1.5.
  • There is no public evidence that the flaw has been exploited, and CISA assessed it as not known to be exploited as of October 30.

Technologies: container-platform, orchestration, cloud-platform

Products: lxd, microcloud, incus

Vendors: canonical, incus

Hackers Steal About $2.7 Million From Polymarket Traders via Hijacked DebugBear Script — Should Read

A DNS compromise at DebugBear caused Polymarket to load a malicious third-party script that hijacked authenticated trading sessions and stole roughly $2.7 million from users. Polymarket removed the script, paused relayer activity, reset sessions, and is refunding affected traders.

  • A compromised DebugBear script loaded by Polymarket on October 29 used signed-in traders’ existing access to sell positions or transfer assets to a hacker-controlled wallet.
  • Polymarket said it is refunding about $2.7 million to 726 affected wallets, while blockchain records showed about $2.64 million in crypto reached the attackers’ wallet in less than an hour.
  • DebugBear said its DNS records were compromised through its domain registrar and that its initial findings indicated the incident targeted one customer website.
  • The malicious code used Polymarket account information and the account’s own transaction-approval mechanism, rather than sending passwords, seed phrases, or private keys to its server.
  • Polymarket removed the script, paused relayer actions, cleared caches, reset active sessions, and referred the incident to law enforcement.

Technologies: network-monitoring, object-storage

Products: debugbear-real-user-monitoring, polymarket, google-cloud-storage

Vendors: debugbear, polymarket, google

NetamLoader Malware Targets Government Windows 10 Systems in Asia via .NET Injection — Should Read

Kaspersky uncovered NetamLoader, a sophisticated .NET-based malware chain targeting a government-only Windows 10 deployment in Asia, likely China, possibly through a supply-chain compromise. It uses AppDomainManager injection, AMSI bypasses, layered payloads, and long-delay C2 polling to run covertly in dllhost.exe.

  • Kaspersky detailed a previously undocumented .NET assembly-loading framework called NetamLoader that targeted a custom Windows 10 build used exclusively by government organizations in Asia.
  • The NetamLoader files were packaged in a CAB archive placed in a Windows Update package directory, although the article says the exact delivery method remains unknown.
  • The infection chain abuses .NET's AppDomainManager mechanism to load malicious code through a legitimate Patch My PC component and uses layered encoded, compressed, or encrypted payloads.
  • The final .NET plugin gathers system information, waits 20 to 40 minutes before contacting the openaigpt4v[.]com command-and-control server, and periodically retrieves XAML files for execution.
  • Kaspersky telemetry identified one victim in Asia, and the activity has not been attributed to a known threat actor or linked conclusively to theft of sensitive information.

Technologies: operating-system

Products: windows-10-china-government-edition, dotnet-framework, patch-my-pc

Vendors: kaspersky, microsoft, patch-my-pc

  • Alpine advised GitLab users to reset their passwords and use the alpinelinux/gitlab:19.3.6 image published October 27, which includes Ruby 3.3.13 and addresses the flaw.

Technologies: operating-system, container-platform, ci-cd, source-control

Products: alpine-linux, gitlab, onigmo, ruby

Vendors: alpine-linux, gitlab

CVSS 10.0 LXD, MicroCloud Flaw Lets Attackers Impersonate Trusted Clients Without a Private Key — Should Read

Canonical patched CVE-2026-112816, a CVSS 10.0 LXD and MicroCloud flaw that lets network-reachable attackers impersonate trusted mTLS clients using only their public certificates. Update LXD and MicroCloud immediately and restrict HTTPS API access until patched.

  • CVE-2026-112816 is a CVSS 10.0 flaw in Canonical LXD and MicroCloud that can allow an attacker to impersonate a trusted client without its private key.
  • The issue occurs because the server checked every certificate supplied by a client against its trust store, even though the connection proves ownership only of the private key for the first certificate.
  • Exploitation requires network access to the HTTPS API and a public certificate for a client that the server already trusts.
  • Canonical released fixed LXD versions 6.10.1, 5.21.9, 5.0.11, and 4.0.15, plus MicroCloud versions 3.4.1 and 2.1.5.
  • There is no public evidence that the flaw has been exploited, and CISA assessed it as not known to be exploited as of October 30.

Technologies: container-platform, orchestration, cloud-platform

Products: lxd, microcloud, incus

Vendors: canonical, incus

Hackers Steal About $2.7 Million From Polymarket Traders via Hijacked DebugBear Script — Should Read

A DNS compromise at DebugBear caused Polymarket to load a malicious third-party script that hijacked authenticated trading sessions and stole roughly $2.7 million from users. Polymarket removed the script, paused relayer activity, reset sessions, and is refunding affected traders.

  • A compromised DebugBear script loaded by Polymarket on October 29 used signed-in traders’ existing access to sell positions or transfer assets to a hacker-controlled wallet.
  • Polymarket said it is refunding about $2.7 million to 726 affected wallets, while blockchain records showed about $2.64 million in crypto reached the attackers’ wallet in less than an hour.
  • DebugBear said its DNS records were compromised through its domain registrar and that its initial findings indicated the incident targeted one customer website.
  • The malicious code used Polymarket account information and the account’s own transaction-approval mechanism, rather than sending passwords, seed phrases, or private keys to its server.
  • Polymarket removed the script, paused relayer actions, cleared caches, reset active sessions, and referred the incident to law enforcement.

Technologies: network-monitoring, object-storage

Products: debugbear-real-user-monitoring, polymarket, google-cloud-storage

Vendors: debugbear, polymarket, google

NetamLoader Malware Targets Government Windows 10 Systems in Asia via .NET Injection — Should Read

Kaspersky uncovered NetamLoader, a sophisticated .NET-based malware chain targeting a government-only Windows 10 deployment in Asia, likely China, possibly through a supply-chain compromise. It uses AppDomainManager injection, AMSI bypasses, layered payloads, and long-delay C2 polling to run covertly in dllhost.exe.

  • Kaspersky detailed a previously undocumented .NET assembly-loading framework called NetamLoader that targeted a custom Windows 10 build used exclusively by government organizations in Asia.
  • The NetamLoader files were packaged in a CAB archive placed in a Windows Update package directory, although the article says the exact delivery method remains unknown.
  • The infection chain abuses .NET's AppDomainManager mechanism to load malicious code through a legitimate Patch My PC component and uses layered encoded, compressed, or encrypted payloads.
  • The final .NET plugin gathers system information, waits 20 to 40 minutes before contacting the openaigpt4v[.]com command-and-control server, and periodically retrieves XAML files for execution.
  • Kaspersky telemetry identified one victim in Asia, and the activity has not been attributed to a known threat actor or linked conclusively to theft of sensitive information.

Technologies: operating-system

Products: windows-10-china-government-edition, dotnet-framework, patch-my-pc

Vendors: kaspersky, microsoft, patch-my-pc

The QR Link With No QR Code in a Calm Telecom Bill Lure — May Read

A calm Hebrew email impersonating Israeli carrier Pelephone hid every link behind a dynamic QR-code service URL, which redirected users to a cloned payment page threatening service suspension. The case shows defenders must follow and continuously evaluate redirect chains and compare displayed links with their real destinations, rather than relying on urgency-based email analysis alone.

  • A Hebrew email impersonating Israeli carrier Pelephone told an employee at an Israeli real-estate investment company to refresh a payment method after a periodic charge failed.
  • Every clickable element in the email, including a footer link displayed as Pelephone’s real web address, pointed to a short link from a commercial dynamic QR-code service despite the message containing no QR code.
  • The short link redirected to a cloned Pelephone page hosted on a third-party Italian IT company’s development subdomain, where a modal warned that an unpaid account could lead to the phone line being blocked.
  • The email itself used calm language without a deadline or suspension threat, while the landing page contained the payment demand and service-blocking warning.
  • IRONSCALES reported that its Malware and URL Protection followed the redirect chain, classified the link as malicious, and automatically quarantined the affected mailbox.

Technologies: email-security

Products: malware-and-url-protection, themis, m365-augmentation

Vendors: ironscales

OpenAI says it's doubling Pro usage limits and bringing Work features to Chat — Optional

OpenAI is testing integration of ChatGPT Work features into regular Chat while unifying ChatGPT and Codex usage under a shared allowance. It has also doubled Work and Codex limits for eligible Pro subscriptions.

  • OpenAI is testing a combined Chat and Work experience with a small group of users before expanding it more broadly.
  • The combined experience is intended to let users move from regular conversations to complex tasks, including working with files and plugins, without switching modes.
  • Codex will remain a separate experience in the ChatGPT desktop app.
  • OpenAI plans to make ChatGPT and Codex draw from a shared usage allowance, while Unlimited Instant usage will not count toward that allowance.
  • OpenAI doubled Work and Codex allowances for Pro 100, Pro 200, and Pro 500 subscriptions effective October 29.

Products: chatgpt, chatgpt-work, codex, chatgpt-pro

Vendors: openai

item.title: Northflank AI API Key Breach and Android CVE-2026-58882 SMS Crash Exploit
item.content:encoded:
Window: 31 Oct 15:00 → 31 Oct 19:00 UTC (4 hours)

Northflank security breach leads to abuse of customers' AI API keys — Should Read

Northflank says a security breach may have exposed and decrypted customer environment variables, with reports of attackers abusing stored AI API keys. Customers should immediately rotate all secrets and review AI-provider usage and billing for unauthorized activity.

  • Northflank warned customers to assume that environment variables stored on its platform had been decrypted and to rotate all credentials and secrets immediately.
  • Multiple Northflank customers reported unauthorized use of AI API keys that they had supplied to the platform.
  • Northflank enabled credential rotation for PostgreSQL, MongoDB, MySQL, and Redis, and enabled audit logs for all customers, including free accounts.
  • Wiz warned Northflank about the incident on October 30, and Northflank subsequently applied multiple network policy patches and sought Wiz incident-response assistance.
  • Wiz identified at least nine security incidents affecting AI development platforms during October, with attackers often seeking environment variables containing AI service credentials.

Technologies: cloud-platform, container-platform, database, secrets-manager

Products: northflank, amazon-bedrock, postgresql, mongodb, mysql, redis

Vendors: northflank, wiz, amazon

New Android SMS of Death exploit can remotely crash unpatched phones — Should Read

A proof-of-concept for Android's "SMS of Death" flaw (CVE-2026-58882) can remotely crash unpatched phones and disrupt cellular and emergency calls using a malformed WAP Push data SMS. Users should install the latest Android security updates, as older Android 12 and 13 devices may remain vulnerable.

  • A proof-of-concept exploit for CVE-2026-58882 can cause unpatched Android phones to lose cellular service or crash when sent a specially crafted text message.
  • The flaw requires no interaction from the target and can interrupt active calls, including emergency calls, before the message appears in the SMS inbox.
  • The issue stems from improper validation in Android's WapPushOverSms.decodeWapPdu function, which can trigger a crash in the com.android.phone process.
  • Google reportedly fixed the flaw in its October 2026 Android security updates for Android 14 through 17, while Android 12 and 13 devices did not receive the fix.
  • Repeated delivery or processing of malicious messages can cause recurring crashes, and testing found that 20 messages could put some phones into reboot loops requiring a factory reset.

Technologies: mobile-os

Products: android, android-debug-bridge

Vendors: google

item.title: Chainalysis Breach and VOLTA Infostealer Highlight AI-Enabled Cybercrime
item.content:encoded:
Window: 31 Oct 11:00 → 31 Oct 15:00 UTC (4 hours)

Chainalysis discloses data breach from "offensive agentic techniques" — Should Read

Chainalysis disclosed that attackers using “offensive agentic techniques” accessed internal systems and customer account metadata, including names, email addresses, user IDs, and role labels. The company says it has found no evidence that investigation data, authentication credentials, or session tokens were exposed.

  • Chainalysis disclosed that an external actor used what it called "offensive agentic techniques" to gain unauthorized access to internal systems and tools earlier in the month.
  • The accessed customer information included user IDs, full names, email addresses, and organizational role labels for platform users.
  • Chainalysis said it has found no evidence so far that investigation content, authentication credentials, or session tokens were accessed.
  • The company is determining which records were accessed for each organization, is patching and hardening its systems, and is working with external cybersecurity experts.
  • Chainalysis advised customers to enable two-factor authentication and be alert for unexpected password resets, authentication prompts, and impersonation scams.

Products: artex

Vendors: chainalysis

Appraisal by AI: Model-driven victim prioritization in the VOLTA infostealer — Should Read

VOLTA-AUTODOXER is a self-deleting Windows infostealer that uses stolen credentials and sessions to build detailed victim dossiers, then sends them to LLMs through OpenRouter to rank assets by criminal monetization value. Its multi-model fallback chain shows attackers are engineering around AI safety refusals to automate post-theft target triage.

  • VOLTA-AUTODOXER is a self-deleting Windows information stealer that collects browser credentials, cookies, payment cards, cryptocurrency wallet data, messaging and gaming sessions, cloud keys, Wi-Fi profiles, and screenshots.
  • After collecting and enriching victim data using stolen sessions, VOLTA creates an Identity_Report.txt file and sends it with a system prompt to OpenRouter for an LLM-generated assessment of the victim’s monetizable assets and security practices.
  • VOLTA uses Claude Opus 4.6 by default and falls back to Kimi K2 and Gemini 2.5 Flash when it detects refusal-style responses such as “I can’t” or “I’m not able.”
  • The malware can use authenticated Gmail, Uber Eats, DoorDash, Discord, and Roblox access to collect additional details such as purchase receipts, order histories, account profiles, and Roblox inventory valuations.
  • VOLTA appears designed for a builder model, with six configuration slots filled at build time for customer-provided settings such as Telegram channels and API keys.

Technologies: browser, operating-system, cloud-platform

Products: openrouter, claude-opus-4-6, kimi-k2, gemini-2-5-flash, google-chrome, windows

Vendors: openrouter, anthropic, moonshot-ai, google, microsoft

Reddit to lock content behind logins to fight scrapers — May Read

Reddit plans to gradually require logins for full access in selected non-U.S. markets, aiming to curb unauthorized content scraping while improving personalization and ad targeting. The front page and individual pages reached through external links are expected to remain accessible without an account.

  • Reddit plans to gradually become a logged-in service and will begin a pilot requiring logins for full access in selected markets outside the United States in the coming months.
  • Reddit has not yet determined which content will be restricted, which countries will be included first, or the rollout timeline.
  • Reddit expects to keep its front page publicly accessible and allow visitors arriving through search or other external links to view the specific page linked by the URL.
  • The company says restricting logged-out access will help address unauthorized content scraping, while AI platforms and search engines can continue to obtain data through commercial licensing agreements.
  • Reddit says it will not require real names or identification documents, plans to re-release a read-only incognito mode in its app, and will let users opt out of personalized advertising.

Products: reddit, reddit-app, reddit-incognito-mode

Vendors: reddit

From Beginner to Bug Hunter: Learning Cybersecurity in the AI Era. — Optional

AI-generated low-quality bug reports have pressured some bounty programs, but learners can still build viable security skills by practicing in authorized labs and submitting evidence-based, reproducible findings. The article promotes TryHackMe as a structured platform for developing these foundations.

  • Curl ended its paid bug bounty program on January 31, 2026, after the share of submitted reports that became confirmed vulnerabilities fell from above 15% in earlier years to below 5% beginning in 2025.
  • Across its lifetime, curl's bug bounty program helped identify 87 confirmed vulnerabilities and paid researchers more than $100,000.
  • Google paused supply chain submissions while leaving outstanding reports unaffected, and its broader vulnerability rewards programs paid researchers $17.1 million in 2025.
  • In April, curl maintainer Daniel Stenberg said report quality had improved, with confirmed vulnerabilities again representing roughly 15% to 16% of submissions despite extensive AI use.
  • The article advises security learners to practice in authorized labs and submit reports with exact reproduction steps, evidence, and clearly demonstrated impact.

Products: tryhackme, cyber-security-101, curl

Vendors: tryhackme, curl, google

item.title: UTA0576 Chains Three Ivanti Connect Secure Flaws for Unauthenticated Root Access
item.content:encoded:
Window: 31 Oct 07:00 → 31 Oct 11:00 UTC (4 hours)

Attackers Chain Three Ivanti Connect Secure Flaws to Gain Unauthenticated Root Access — Must Read

CISA added two Ivanti Connect Secure flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog after attackers chained them with an authentication bypass to obtain unauthenticated root-level code execution. Organizations should update ICS to 25.1.1.3 or 22.8R2.6 immediately.

  • CISA added CVE-2026-111357 and CVE-2026-118527, two Ivanti Connect Secure flaws under active exploitation, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
  • Threat actor UTA0576 chained those two flaws with the authentication-bypass issue CVE-2026-104935 to achieve unauthenticated root-level code execution on Ivanti Connect Secure.
  • Rather than deploying web shells or malware, UTA0576 was observed extracting credentials and limited Active Directory metadata, conducting host reconnaissance, and searching for administrator passwords and BitLocker recovery keys.
  • Ivanti released fixes in Ivanti Connect Secure 25.1.1.3 and 22.8R2.6, which address all vulnerabilities exploited in the chain.
  • Federal Civilian Executive Branch agencies must remediate CVE-2026-111357 by November 2, 2026, and CVE-2026-118527 by November 13, 2026.

Technologies: vpn, remote-access

Products: ivanti-connect-secure

Vendors: ivanti
